statement: "Dungka!" (stylized in all uppercase) is a song recorded by the Filipino boy band SB19 for their third extended play (EP), Simula at Wakas (2025).
The band's leader, Pablo, wrote the song and co-produced it with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase.
It is an pop diss track aimed at haters, with lyrics demanding them to leave, uttering the phrase "doon ka" (lit. 'go over there').
"Dungka!" is listed as the sixth track on the EP, which Sony Music Philippines released on April 25, 2025.
"Dungka!" received favorable reviews from music critics, who complimented Pablo's songwriting and his use of wordplay.
The song was an entry to record charts.
It peaked at number 21 on the Philippines Hot 100.
It peaked at number 7 on Billboard's World Digital Song Sales.

The accompanying music video, directed by Kerbs Balagtas, featured Filipino culture and depicted the band in the streets showing allegiance to their community while opposing an antagonist who threatened the locals.
SB19 promoted the song with live performances and included it on the set list of their Simula at Wakas World Tour (2025).
"Dungka!" received multiple accolades, including a Filipino Music Award for Pop Song of the Year.
The Filipino boy band SB19 released their first extended play (EP), Pagsibol (lit. 'growth'), in 2021.
Pagsibol explored genres such as pop rock, hip-hop, and EDM.
Pagsibol departed from the dance-pop production from their debut studio album, Get in the Zone (2020).
Pablo, the band's leader, revealed in an interview with Zach Sang that Pagsibol and their future releases are part of a trilogy.
The trilogy includes Pagtatag! (lit. 'strengthening') and Simula at Wakas (lit. 'beginning and end').
In 2023, the group released their second EP, Pagtatag!, which is the trilogy's second installment.
The EP Pagtatag! includes the single, "Gento" (2023).
"Gento" scored their first entry to two record charts, including in the Philippines.
In the Philippines, "Gento" peaked at number eight.
The following year, they confirmed during the premiere night for Pagtatag!: The Documentary (2024) that they are currently working with Simula at Wakas.
On January 31, 2025, SB19 published a trailer via their social media accounts.
In the trailer, they revealed the title of their third EP, Simula and Wakas.
In the trailer, they announced its release date.
The EP's lead single, "Dam", was released ahead of the EP on February 28.
"Dam" achieved commercial success.
On April 7, the band announced the EP's track list, along with the names of the songwriters and producers involved in the record.
Out of seven tracks in the EP, "Dungka!" is listed as track six.
Sony Music Philippines released Simula at Wakas on April 25 through digital download and streaming formats.
"Dungka!" is 3 minutes and 35 seconds in length.
Pablo, the band's leader, wrote the song by himself.
Pablo co-produced the song with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase.
Pablo and Joshua Daniel Nase also mixed and mastered the song together.
The song's title, "Dungka!", is a wordplay derived from the Tagalog phrase "doon ka".
"Doon ka" translates to "go over there" in English.
"Doon ka" served as a refrain in the song's lyrics.
Musically, "Dungka!" is a pop song with elements of techno, hyperpop and rave music.
"Dungka!" is accompanied by catchy pounding beats.
Rome Saenz of Billboard Philippines described the song's production as "blaring [and] sharp".
Rafael Bautista of Nylon Manila and Preview's Kyla Villena described the song's production as "loud".
Lyrically, "Dungka!" is interpreted as a diss track against SB19's haters.
"Dungka!" responds to the criticisms and name-calling imposed on them.
"Dungka!" responds to those who are doubting their capabilities.
In the lyrics, the phrase "doon ka" is prominent.
"Doon ka" is a common Filipino expression that signifies displeasure.
"Doon ka" was used in the song to convey that negativity and undesirable people are unwelcome and should leave.
Other lyrics also follow a similar theme, like "Kung 'di mo 'to gusto, tumabi ka d'yan" (lit. 'If you do not like this, move out of the way').
The lyric "Kung 'di mo 'to gusto, tumabi ka d'yan" further insists that their critics should go away.
"Dungka!" received favorable reviews from music critics.
Many critics complimented Pablo's songwriting.
Kathleen Llemit, writing for The Philippine Star, noted Pablo's preference for using wordplay.
Kathleen Llemit considers Pablo's use of wordplay a "testament to [his] songwriting skills".
Ann Jenireene Gomez of the Daily Tribune described the use of wordplay "witty".
Ann Jenireene Gomez described the use of wordplay as a "cheeky way to shoo away negative energy".
Dayne Aduna of VMan Southeast Asia regarded the wordplay as a playful way to alter an everyday Filipino phrase.
The song's noisy production was also a key topic.
Critics noted that, despite it sounding loud, Nylon Manila's Rafael Bautista opined that the noise still resonates in a good way.
Rome Saenz of Billboard Philippines considered the song "irresistibly catchy", despite its noisy production.
Inquirer's Pauline Miranda compared "Dungka!" with the group's 2021 single "Bazinga".
Pauline Miranda referred to "Dungka!" as "Bazinga's" "more fun [and] unbothered brother".
Bandwagon's Hidzir Junaini opined that "Dungka!" is a surprising track in the EP.
Bautista finds "Dungka!" as one of the tracks that stood out from Simula at Wakas.
Commercially, "Dungka!" was an entry for SB19 on record charts upon the release of Simula at Wakas.
In the Philippines, the song entered two Billboard Philippines charts.
"Dungka!" debuted and peaked at number 21 on the Philippines Hot 100 during the week of May 10, 2025.
"Dungka!" debuted and peaked at number 14 on the Top Philippine Songs during the week of May 10, 2025.
The song spent a total of 12 weeks on the Philippines Hot 100.
The song spent 3 weeks on the Top Philippine Songs charts.
In the same week, the song debuted and peaked at number seven on Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart.
This marked SB19's third entry on the Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart.
The previous entries on Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart were "Gento" and "Dam".
Kerbs Balagtas directed the accompanying music video for "Dungka!".
The music video was surprise-released on April 25, 2025, on YouTube.
The release date of the music video was the same day as the release of Simula at Wakas.
The music video is themed around street credibility.
The music video is set in the chaotic streets of Metro Manila.
The music video depicts SB19 showing their allegiance to the local community.
In the video, SB19 were circumventing around the antagonist, played by social media personality Ghost Wrecker.
The antagonist taunts and threatens the locals in the video.
People later come together to oppose the antagonist in the video.
The video also showed activities relevant to the Filipino culture, including Zumba, street food, activism, street basketball, karaoke, ten-twenty, and band members participating in a battle rap.
The group also gathered together to raise social awareness in the video.

They raised posters and signs with text including "Iangat ang sining na Pilipino" (lit. 'Elevate Filipino art') and "Sining ang sandata sa kulturang mapagpalaya" (lit. 'Art is the weapon in a liberating culture').
The music video received favorable reviews for depicting Filipino culture.
It was regarded as a tribute to individuality, community, diversity, and everyday life.
It was regarded as calling out negativity and raising one's voice for change.
Writers highlighted a scene from the video where the antagonist was eating a crab.
They interpreted the crab-eating scene as a symbol for crab mentality among Filipinos.
The video featured a large number of celebrity cameos.
Rafael Bautista of Nylon Manila considered it the band's "most star-studded music video".

Aside from Ghost Wrecker, the ensemble cast includes comedian Vice Ganda, actress and singer Maymay Entrata, Ben&Ben members Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma, rappers Shehyee and Smugglaz, cosplayer Alodia Gosiengfiao, gamer Jayat, and social media personalities Kween Yasmin, Malupiton, Mimiyuuuh, and Sassa Gurl.
All listed celebrities collaborated with the band to help spread a message about diversity and uniqueness among people, including those in the LGBTQ community.
Following the release of Simula at Wakas, SB19 arranged a surprise flash mob in Bonifacio Global City in Taguig on April 25.
SB19 performed "Dungka!" with "Dam" during the flash mob.
The band followed it with a television performance of "Dungka!" during their appearance on the variety show It's Showtime on April 26.
On May 7, the group appeared on the Wish 107.5 Bus.
They performed a three-song set list on the Wish 107.5 Bus.
The set list included "Dungka!".
They performed "Dungka!" on a makeshift stage outside the bus.
In support of the EP, SB19 embarked on their third world tour, the Simula at Wakas World Tour (2025).
"Dungka!" was included on the set list of the Simula at Wakas World Tour (2025).
SB19 appeared at the Hito Music Awards 2025 in Taiwan on June 21.
SB19 performed the song during the Hito Music Awards 2025 ceremony.
The band went to Rome, Italy.
The band served as a guest performer at the Sama sa Roma 2025 event on October 12.
"Dungka!" was among the songs they performed at Sama sa Roma 2025.
On November 30, the group performed the song during their halftime show at the Honor of Kings International Championship 2025.
The Honor of Kings International Championship 2025 was held at the Ayala Malls Manila Bay in Parañaque.
Shortly after, they went to Kaohsiung, Taiwan.
They performed at the ACON 2025 festival held at the Kaohsiung National Stadium on December 7.
They performed four songs at the ACON 2025 festival, including "Dungka!".
A snippet of the song was featured in a video uploaded in June by FIFA on TikTok.
The song was also featured in a music video for the 2025 video game Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.
Credits are adapted from the song's music video.
